NAT rules perform address translation, and network rules are intended for Layer 3/4 address, port, and protocol filtering.

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant with the following configurations:  
  
- User consent for applications is disabled.  
- Only administrators can grant permissions to applications.  
  
You register an application named App1 that uses delegated Microsoft Graph permissions.  
  
You need to configure App1 to meet the following requirements:  
  
- Enable user sign-ins without interactive consent prompts.  
- Enable App1 to access Microsoft Graph on behalf of the signed-in user.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure enterprise applications to require user assignment and assign users to App1.
Modify the app registration to use application permissions instead of delegated permissions.
Add the required delegated Microsoft Graph permissions to the app registration and rely on user consent during sign-in.
Grant admin consent to App1 for the required delegated permissions.

questions.explanation:
Delegated permissions allow an application to access Microsoft Graph on behalf of the signed-in user. When user consent is disabled, an administrator must grant consent; granting tenant-wide admin consent to the required delegated permissions lets users sign in without being prompted to consent.

**Learn more:** [Consent experience for applications in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/application-consent-experience) · [Overview of permissions and consent in the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/permissions-consent-overview)

Microsoft Defender for Containers is enabled for Sub1, and runtime protection is active on cluster1.  
  
Your company’s developers deploy pods with elevated privileges, and those deployments are created in cluster1.  
  
You need to prevent pods with elevated privileges from being accepted by cluster1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an Azure policy for cluster1.
Enable agentless discovery for Kubernetes in Defender for Containers.
Configure runtime threat protection alerts for privileged container activity.
Enable vulnerability assessment for images in ACR1.

questions.explanation:
Azure Policy for Kubernetes can enforce admission controls in AKS. Its built-in policy, **Kubernetes cluster should not allow privileged containers**, prevents creation of privileged containers, whereas Defender runtime protection detects activity after deployment and image vulnerability assessment evaluates image vulnerabilities.

**Learn more:** [Built-in policy definitions for Azure Kubernetes Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/policy-reference) · [Kubernetes data plane hardening](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/kubernetes-workload-protections)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two management groups, **MG1** and **MG2**, which contain multiple Azure subscriptions. The subscriptions are associated with a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You have a user named **User1** and a global administrator named **Admin1**.  
  
You learn that User1 created an Azure subscription named **Sub1** under the **MG2** management group and is its only owner.  
  
You need to ensure that Admin1 can remove User1's Owner role on Sub1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Assign Admin1 the User Access Administrator role for Sub1.
Instruct Admin1 to use Privileged Identity Management (PIM) to request the Security Administrator role.
Instruct Admin1 to enable Access management for Azure resources.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra Global Administrator does not automatically have Azure RBAC access to every subscription. Enabling **Access management for Azure resources** elevates the signed-in Global Administrator by assigning the Azure **User Access Administrator** role at the root scope. That role permits management of role assignments across subscriptions and management groups in the tenant, including removal of User1’s Owner assignment on Sub1.

**Learn more:** [Elevate access to manage all Azure subscriptions and management groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin) · [Azure roles, Microsoft Entra roles, and classic subscription administrator roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/rbac-and-directory-admin-roles)

questions.explanation:

Creating storage2 with an account encryption key permits a Fabrikam-managed key from Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM to encrypt the account’s services, including Table storage. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure management group named MG1 that includes two subscriptions named Sub1 and Sub2. Both subscriptions are connected to a Microsoft Entra tenant that includes a security group named Group1.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Overview  
  
Fabrikam, Inc. is a consulting company with a main office in New York City and branch offices in Amsterdam and Singapore.  
  
Existing Environment — Network environment  
  
The on-premises network has a datacenter in each office.  
  
Existing Environment — Cloud environment  
  
Fabrikam has two Azure subscriptions named Sub1 and Sub2, plus a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes Microsoft 365 E5 licenses.  
  
All subscriptions are linked to a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com that contains the identities shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784319340464-1t88k4v1.png)  
  
The tenant contains the groups shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784319342834-if549ztu.png)  
  
All devices are enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
Existing Environment — Sub1 Resources  
  
Sub1 contains a resource group named RG1, which contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784319345334-tjz13zoq.png)  
  
SQLServer1 uses Microsoft SQL Server authentication.  
  
Sub1 has an Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) named WAF1 with the following rule-set types:  
  
- Bot Manager 1.1  
- Azure-managed Default Rule Set (DRS)  
  
Sub1 has the following compliance standards assigned in Microsoft Defender for Cloud:  
  
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4  
- Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB)  
- System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2 Type 2  
  
Existing Environment — Sub2 Resources  
  
Sub2 contains a resource group named RG2.  
  
Planned Changes and Requirements — Planned Changes  
  
Fabrikam plans to make the following changes:  
  
- Deploy the following key vaults to RG1:  
  - AKV2 in the West Europe Azure region  
  - AKV3 in the Central US Azure region  
  - AKV4 in the East US Azure region  
- Deploy the following key vaults to RG2:  
  - AKV5 in the East US region  
- Configure VM1 to read data from storage1.  
- Create function apps with the following hosting plans:  
  - Fa1: Flex Consumption hosting plan  
  - Fa2: Consumption hosting plan  
  - Fa3: Dedicated hosting plan  
- For WAF1, implement rate-limiting rules based on request location.  
- Enable the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 compliance standard in Defender for Cloud.  
- Create a new storage account named storage2 that supports Azure Table storage.  
- Enforce multifactor authentication (MFA) when database administrators access SQLdb1.  
- Implement ExpressRoute circuits to the on-premises network as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784319347618-wju575ao.png)  
  
For RG1, create a new Privileged Identity Management (PIM) eligible role assignment that assigns the Contributor role to supported groups.  
  
Planned Changes and Requirements — Technical Requirements  
  
Fabrikam has the following technical requirements:  
  
- If VM1 is deleted, its permissions must be removed automatically.  
- The AKS1 managed identity must only be able to pull images from Registry1.  
- The ID1 managed identity must be able to push images to and pull images from Registry1.  
- All data in the storage accounts must be encrypted by using Fabrikam-managed keys.  
- All outbound traffic from the function apps to the on-premises network must use ExpressRoute circuits.  
- ExpressRoute connectivity between the on-premises network and the Azure environment must be encrypted by using Layer 2 or Layer 3 encryption.  
  
You need to delegate a user to implement the planned change for Defender for Cloud. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which user should you select?
questions.explanation:
Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance standards are implemented as Azure Policy initiatives, and adding a standard requires Owner or Policy Contributor permissions at the target scope. Admin1’s Resource Policy Contributor assignment on Sub1 is the least-privileged listed assignment that permits this policy operation. [Microsoft Learn: Assign regulatory compliance standards in Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are setting up a new Microsoft Sentinel workspace called Workspace1.

You need to ensure that Workspace1 creates service tickets in the ITSM system for every new security incident.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Sentinel playbook is an Azure Logic Apps workflow that can be triggered for newly created incidents and can call an external ITSM system’s connector or API to create tickets. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure key vault named KV1 that uses role-based access control (RBAC) authorization. KV1 contains database connection strings for an Azure App Service web app named App1.  
  
You enable a firewall on KV1 and permit access to KV1 only from the virtual network that contains App1.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 can retrieve secrets from KV1 without using credentials kept in the application configuration.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
A managed identity lets an Azure App Service obtain Microsoft Entra ID tokens for Azure Key Vault without storing credentials in the application configuration. For a Key Vault configured for RBAC authorization, assign that identity the Key Vault Secrets User role so it can read secrets.

**Learn more:** [Use Key Vault references as app settings in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-key-vault-references) · [Managed Identities for Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-managed-identity)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a hunting query.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Sentinel hunting query supports proactive investigation and searching across security data, but it does not automatically modify new incidents. Automatically assigning newly created incidents and adding a triage tag requires an automation rule triggered when an incident is created; automation rules can assign incident ownership and add tags.\
\
**Learn more:** [Automate threat response in Microsoft Sentinel with automation rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automate-incident-handling-with-automation-rules) · [Hunting capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/hunting)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a playbook.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel automation rules apply actions when incidents are created and can automatically assign and tag incidents. A playbook is a workflow that must be run manually or triggered, commonly by an automation rule; creating it by itself does not guarantee that every new incident is immediately assigned and marked for triage.\
\
**Learn more:** [Automation in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/automation) · [Automate threat response in Microsoft Sentinel with automation rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automate-incident-handling-with-automation-rules)

questions.question:
Solution: Create an automation rule.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel automation rules can be applied when incidents are created and can automatically assign an incident to an owner or group and add tags. A rule with an incident-created trigger can therefore assign every new incident to the Tier 1 analysts group and label it for triage.\
\
**Learn more:** [Automation in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/automation) · [Automate threat response in Microsoft Sentinel with automation rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automate-incident-handling-with-automation-rules)

questions.question:
Solution: You create an analytics rule.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules generate alerts and incidents, whereas automation rules perform incident-handling actions such as assigning incident ownership and adding tags. Creating only an analytics rule therefore cannot immediately assign each new incident to the Tier 1 analysts group and flag it for triage.\
\
**Learn more:** [Automate threat response in Microsoft Sentinel with automation rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automate-incident-handling-with-automation-rules) · [Create scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules)

Which Defender plan should you enable?

Microsoft Defender for SQL Servers on Machines
Microsoft Defender for Azure SQL Databases

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Open-Source Relational Databases provides threat protection for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. The other listed plans protect different resource types, so enabling them would not provide the required PostgreSQL coverage and could add unnecessary cost.

Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A user-assigned managed identity can be assigned to more than one virtual machine and authorized to access a target service through Azure RBAC. A suitable role assignment on storage1 grants both VMs access when their workloads authenticate by using the shared user-assigned managed identity.\
\

questions.explanation:
A system-assigned managed identity can receive an Azure RBAC role assignment. Assigning each VM identity an appropriate role scoped to the storage account authorizes access to that storage account.\
\
**Learn more:** [Authorize operations for data access - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/authorize-data-access) · [Assign Azure roles using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal)

questions.explanation:
System-assigned managed identities have Microsoft Entra service principals that can be included in a security group. Assigning an Azure RBAC role on a storage account to that group grants the role’s storage permissions to the managed identities of both virtual machines. Permission changes involving managed identities and group membership can take time to propagate because of caching.\
\
**Learn more:** [Managed identity best practice recommendations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/managed-identity-best-practice-recommendations) · [Managed identities for Azure resources FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/managed-identities-faq)

questions.question:

Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure private endpoint supplies private network connectivity but does not authorize managed identities to access Azure Storage data. Access for a VM's managed identity requires an appropriate Azure RBAC role assignment, and clients must also be able to route to and resolve the private endpoint. A private endpoint alone therefore does not ensure access for both virtual machines.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Azure portal to grant a managed identity access to a resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/grant-managed-identity-resource-access-azure-portal) · [Connect to a storage account using an Azure Private Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/tutorial-private-endpoint-storage-portal)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Storage account named `storage1` that contains Azure Files shares.  
  
You have an application named App1 that uses a system-assigned managed identity to access the shares.  
  
Administrators access the shares by using storage account keys.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 can access the shares without using the storage account keys. What should you do on `storage1`?

options.text: Store the storage account access keys in Azure Key Vault and regenerate them periodically.
Set Allow storage account key access to Disabled.
Select Default to Microsoft Entra authorization in the Azure portal.
Assign the Storage File Data Privileged Reader role to the managed identity of App1.

questions.explanation:
A system-assigned managed identity is a Microsoft Entra service principal that can be granted Azure RBAC permissions instead of being given a storage account key. The Storage File Data Privileged Reader role grants read access to Azure Files while overriding existing ACLs, allowing the identity to authorize its file-data access through Microsoft Entra ID. Disabling storage-account-key access would reject the administrators’ key-based requests, and the portal’s Microsoft Entra default does not configure an application’s authorization.

**Learn more:** [Enable Access to Azure File Shares Using OAuth Over REST](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/authorize-oauth-rest) · [Assign Share-Level Permissions for Azure Files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-identity-assign-share-level-permissions)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Overview -  
  
Fabrikam, Inc. is a consulting company. The company has its main office in New York City and branch offices in Amsterdam and Singapore.  
  
Existing Environment. Network environment  
  
The on-premises network has a datacenter in each office.  
  
Existing Environment. Cloud environment  
  
Fabrikam has two Azure subscriptions named Sub1 and Sub2, plus a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes Microsoft 365 E5 licenses.

SQLServer1 uses Microsoft SQL Server authentication.

Existing Environment. Sub2 Resources

Planned Changes and Requirements. Planned Changes  
  
Fabrikam plans to make the following changes:  
  
- Deploy the following key vaults to RG1:  
  - AKV2 in the West Europe Azure region  
  - AKV3 in the Central US Azure region  
  - AKV4 in the East US Azure region  
- Deploy the following key vault to RG2:  
  - AKV5 in the East US region -

options.text: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM)

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Microsoft Security Copilot.  
  
Users are assigned either the Security Copilot Contributor role or the Security Copilot Owner role.  
  
A contributor enables an unapproved custom plugin, and some Security Copilot capabilities in embedded experiences no longer work.  
  
You need to ensure that only owners can add plugins that affect all users.  
  
What should you configure in **Plugin settings**?

options.text: Select Contributors and Owners to configure which users can add custom plugins at the user scope.
Select Contributors and Owners to configure which users can add custom plugins at the workspace scope.
Select Owners only to configure which users can add custom plugins at the workspace scope.
Select Owners only to configure which users can add custom plugins at the user scope.

questions.explanation:
Custom plugins that affect all users are governed at the workspace-wide scope. Configuring **Owners only** for who can add and manage custom plugins for users in the workspace prevents contributors from publishing or managing plugins that affect everyone. Microsoft documents this setting as restricting organization-wide custom-plugin management to owners.

**Learn more:** [Manage plugins in Microsoft Security Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/manage-plugins)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning to deploy Microsoft 365 Copilot.

What should you create?

options.text: a Microsoft Purview data loss prevention (DLP) policy in audit mode for SharePoint Online
a Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) remediation action
a Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication (MFA) for SharePoint Online
a SharePoint Advanced Management (SAM) Data access governance report

questions.explanation:
A SharePoint Advanced Management (SAM) Data access governance report can identify content shared with **Everyone except external users**, the built-in SharePoint group representing all internal users. Its reports track SharePoint sites where content has broad internal sharing exposure.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Foundry project that includes a model deployment named Deployment1.  
  
Deployment1 includes an agent named Agent1 that uses an existing default guardrail configuration.  
  
You discover that Agent1 produces tool calls containing harmful language.  
  
You need to ensure that Agent1 responses with harmful content are blocked from running. The solution must prevent changes to the Deployment1 configuration.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an automatic evaluation of the dataset of Agent1.
Create a custom guardrail and assign it directly to Agent1.
Create a red teaming run for Agent1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Foundry guardrails support an agent-specific tool-call intervention point with an annotate-and-block action. Assigning a custom guardrail directly to the agent overrides the guardrail inherited from its underlying model deployment, allowing harmful tool-call content to be blocked without changing the deployment configuration.

**Learn more:** [Guardrails and controls overview in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview?view=foundry) · [Intervention points concepts - Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/intervention-points)

DSPM recommendations can create DLP policies to mitigate oversharing risks, and those policies are managed and edited in the DLP solution.

**Learn more:** [Take action with Data Security Posture Management recommendations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/data-security-posture-management-recommendations) · [Learn about data loss prevention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/purview/dlp-learn-about-dlp)

VM1 hosts an application that accesses storage1. A different application accesses storage1 from the public IP address `xxx.xxx.xx.xx`.  
  
For storage1, you configure **Public network access** as **Enabled from selected virtual networks and IP addresses**. You add an IP network rule for `xxx.xxx.xx.xx`.

You need to ensure that both VM1 and `xxx.xxx.xx.xx` can access storage1 through the public endpoint, while blocking all other access.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set Public network access to Enabled from all networks.
Enable a private endpoint for storage1.
Add a public IP address to VM1.
Enable the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint for Subnet1.

questions.explanation:
Azure Storage network rules can allow access to the public endpoint from selected IP address ranges and selected virtual-network subnets. To allow VM1 in Subnet1 without opening the storage account to other networks, Subnet1 must expose the `Microsoft.Storage` service endpoint; the subnet can then be allowed as a virtual-network rule. The existing IP network rule continues to allow `xxx.xxx.xx.xx`, and all other sources remain denied.

**Learn more:** [Azure Storage firewall rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-network-security) · [Azure virtual network service endpoints overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview)
